title: Partial Label Learning with Semantic Label Representations

problem.claim: Partial-label learning must identify the ground-truth label from a candidate label set for each training instance.

gap.claim: Existing PLL methods learn plain representations through coarse supervision and may fail to capture sufficiently distinguishable representations under severe label ambiguity, especially when candidate labels have similar visual patterns.

contributions.claim: ParSE combines visual-semantic representation learning with label disambiguation for partial-label learning.

The weighted calibration rank loss uses disambiguated label confidence to weight image-feature and semantic-label similarity across candidates and models ranking relations between candidate and non-candidate labels.
The learned visual-semantic representations support subsequent label disambiguation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe ParSE as a novel framework and the weighted calibration rank loss as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on benchmarks show that ParSE outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts, according to the authors.

narrative_sequence.summary: PLL identifies the ground-truth label within each instance's candidate label set.
Efficient feature representations are needed to facilitate label disambiguation.
Existing coarse-supervision representations are insufficiently distinguishable under difficult label ambiguity.
ParSE introduces visual-semantic representation learning and label disambiguation, including a weighted calibration rank loss.
The authors report that ParSE outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts on benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The method weights image-feature and semantic-label similarity using disambiguated label confidence and accounts for candidate versus non-candidate ranking.

interpretation.claim: Confidence-aware semantic alignment may help distinguish labels that share similar visual patterns.

application.claim: For ambiguous classification settings, combine confidence-weighted representation learning with explicit ranking information among plausible and implausible labels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported benchmark experiments or to ambiguity types other than similar visual patterns.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, or quantitative performance margins.
The abstract does not describe the training procedure, computational requirements, or ablation results.
